For every $p,q\ge2$, the standard level space supported in the first row and column, of dimension $p+q-3$, admits no proper linear level-space extension. Each of its two conjugate non-real three-dimensional matrix summands has exactly twenty-four level lines, the cone over the ordinary flexes of Klein's quartic. Their direct sum contains no level space of dimension three, and a level space containing one of these pure lines has dimension one. If there is no such index, then $h(X)=\infty$. For every fixed prime $p$ and fixed positive integer $r$, deciding $h(X)=r$ belongs to $\mathrm{Mod}_p\mathrm P$. The cases $r=1,2$ are complete for that class, and at $p=2$ the case $r=3$ is $\oplus\mathrm P$-complete even under the promise $h(X)\ge3$. The exact-height function, including the output $\infty$, is computable deterministically with $\operatorname{poly}(L)$ work bits, where $L$ is the circuit input length, and therefore in $2^{\operatorname{poly}(L)}$ time. This upper bound also permits a binary-encoded input prime. Under this uniform convention the function is $\#\mathrm P$-hard by polynomially many nonadaptive oracle calls, even on inputs of height at least two. With a unary-encoded prime, promised height-two decision is oracle-equivalent to exact counting as stated in Theorem~\ref{thm:uniform-counting}.
